scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic child process inherits the parent's generator state and emits a final same-scope nonce already consumed by the parent because child diversification or reseed is absent.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled deterministic PRNG fixture with synthetic keys and a mock read-only consumer records only generated test values and same-scope duplicate receipts.
scenarios.positive_control: The same fork simulation with explicit child diversification or reseed produces a distinct final nonce stream while preserving the same synthetic key and consumer.
scenarios.negative_control: Parent and child use independently rotated synthetic key scopes; repeated raw values are then classified as cross-scope and must not satisfy the same-scope reuse oracle.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture would expose production tokens, leave the local owned sandbox, require live prediction against real systems, or use unauthorized secrets.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding child creation to a fresh reseed/diversification generation, parent and child no longer produce a forbidden same-key final nonce duplicate in repeated deterministic runs.
scenarios.value_property_security_scope: Classify the value as a nonce requiring same-key non-repetition, bind both outputs to the same synthetic key/session security scope, and record consumer acceptance.
scenarios.generator_seed_entropy_reseed: Record generator implementation, parent state generation, synthetic seed identity, entropy fixture, absent child reseed epoch, and repaired child reseed/diversification generation.
scenarios.fork_snapshot_restart_lifecycle: Bind parent process generation, fork identity, copied state, child process generation, first child output, and whether diversification occurs before any value consumption.
scenarios.counter_namespace_reservation: Record that no independent counter namespace or reservation layer adds uniqueness in this case, preventing an allocator from masking the cloned-generator relation.
scenarios.persistence_crash_restart: Record that persistence and restart are held constant and unused for the causal assertion so the duplicate cannot be attributed to restored checkpoint state.
scenarios.transform_encoding_truncation: Use an identity encoding with fixed width for both parent and child values and prove the raw duplicate remains the exact final consumed nonce.
scenarios.consumer_construction_identity: Identify the mock construction consumer, synthetic key identity, required nonce non-repetition rule, and receipts showing both duplicate final values are consumed.
scenarios.effective_randomness_lifecycle_capabilit: The demonstrated capability is limited to deterministic same-scope nonce reuse after a controlled fork with cloned generator state and absent child diversification.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only duplicate marker over synthetic nonce values and synthetic keys, with no ciphertext recovery, token authority, or external action.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate parent/child process generations, generator state, seed/reseed epochs, security scope, both final nonce values, consumer identity, and duplicate receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold generator implementation, synthetic seed, key scope, consumer, and fork point constant while changing only absent versus present child reseed/diversification.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject independent key scopes, hidden child reseed, display-only truncation, duplicate logging, post-generation domain separation, or a receipt from another process generation.
scenarios.evidence_level: NRL3 because a mock read-only consumer accepts the same final nonce twice under one synthetic key scope after the controlled fork lifecycle boundary.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: NRL3 maximum until a bounded reversible construction effect plus complete fork, state, consumer, counterfactual, and remediation evidence supports NRL4 or NRL5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic nonce counter restores an older persistence checkpoint after restart and reissues a value that was already consumed before the crash in the same namespace and key scope.
scenarios.safe_oracle: An in-memory fake persistence journal, bounded counter namespace, synthetic key, and mock consumer emit only deterministic counter and duplicate receipts with no real token use.
scenarios.positive_control: When the current checkpoint is durably advanced after each consumed allocation, restart resumes beyond every prior consumed counter value and the duplicate oracle remains false.
scenarios.negative_control: The same stale checkpoint is restored under a new independent synthetic key/session namespace, demonstrating that counter-number repetition alone is not same-scope reuse.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture would expose production tokens, leave the local owned sandbox, require live prediction against real systems, or use unauthorized secrets.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After write-ahead reservation or durable checkpoint ordering is fixed, controlled restart never reissues a counter value previously consumed in the same synthetic scope.
scenarios.value_property_security_scope: Classify the value as a same-key nonce/sequence requiring non-repetition, bind pre-crash and post-restart values to one counter namespace and synthetic key generation.
scenarios.generator_seed_entropy_reseed: Record the hybrid generator identity, deterministic seed fixture, unchanged seed/reseed state, and prove the causal variable is counter persistence rather than entropy.
scenarios.fork_snapshot_restart_lifecycle: Bind controlled crash identity, restart generation, restored counter state, unchanged security scope, and first post-restart allocation before any unrelated state change.
scenarios.counter_namespace_reservation: Record namespace identity, counter generation, allocation identity, pre-crash consumed value, stale restored value, reservation state, and post-restart duplicate allocation.
scenarios.persistence_crash_restart: Trace counter mutation, persistence intent, durable checkpoint lag, consumed value receipt, controlled crash, restored checkpoint, and repeated post-restart consumed value.
scenarios.transform_encoding_truncation: Use a lossless deterministic encoding so raw counter identity and final consumed nonce remain equal; no truncation or encoding collision is involved.
scenarios.consumer_construction_identity: Identify the mock consumer and synthetic key scope that accept both pre-crash and post-restart values, producing a read-only same-scope reuse receipt.
scenarios.effective_randomness_lifecycle_capabilit: The demonstrated capability is limited to reissuing one already-consumed synthetic nonce value after deterministic restart from a stale persistence checkpoint.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an in-memory journal and duplicate-consumption receipt; no real protocol traffic, production nonce, or cryptographic secret is involved.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind counter namespace, security scope, persistence checkpoint generation, crash/restart identity, both consumed values, consumer, and duplicate receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold generator, key scope, consumer, counter width, and crash point constant while changing only stale versus current durable persistence checkpoint generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject new key/session scope, unconsumed pre-crash allocation, stale telemetry, duplicate logging, transform-added uniqueness, or another restart generation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: NRL4 because a reversible in-memory persistence fixture causes a bounded same-scope duplicate-consumption effect across a controlled crash/restart transition.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: NRL4 maximum until complete persistence ordering, alternative elimination, counterfactuals, receipt binding, and remediation replay satisfy regression-verified NRL5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Two synthetic workers receive overlapping reservation ranges from the same nonce namespace and both consume the same final counter-derived nonce under one security scope.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled fake allocator with a bounded in-memory namespace and mock read-only consumers records only reservation ranges and synthetic consumed values.
scenarios.positive_control: An atomic non-overlapping reservation allocator assigns disjoint ranges to both workers and every consumed final nonce remains unique in the same synthetic key scope.
scenarios.negative_control: Overlapping numeric ranges allocated to different independent synthetic key namespaces do not satisfy the same-scope duplicate oracle even when counter numbers match.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture would expose production tokens, leave the local owned sandbox, require live prediction against real systems, or use unauthorized secrets.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After atomic reservation or namespace partitioning is applied, repeated deterministic schedules never allocate overlapping consumed values in the same scope.
scenarios.value_property_security_scope: Classify values as counter-derived nonces requiring same-key non-repetition and bind both workers to the same synthetic key, namespace, and consumer scope.
scenarios.generator_seed_entropy_reseed: Record generator identity, deterministic seed and reseed state, and prove random seed behavior is held constant while reservation allocation is the causal variable.
scenarios.fork_snapshot_restart_lifecycle: Record worker/process generations and prove no fork-state clone, restart, or snapshot restoration independently creates the duplicate relation.
scenarios.counter_namespace_reservation: Bind counter namespace, reservation generation, each worker's allocation operation, synchronization identity, overlapping ranges, consumed element, and duplicate relation.
scenarios.persistence_crash_restart: Keep the fake persistence checkpoint current and identical across controls so crash/restart state cannot explain the reservation overlap or duplicate consumption.
scenarios.transform_encoding_truncation: Use a one-to-one counter encoding without truncation so the overlapping raw counter element becomes exactly the duplicate final consumed nonce.
scenarios.consumer_construction_identity: Identify both mock consumers or calls into the same synthetic construction scope and record deterministic receipts showing the overlapping value is consumed twice.
scenarios.effective_randomness_lifecycle_capabilit: The demonstrated capability is limited to duplicate consumption of one synthetic counter-derived nonce caused by overlapping same-namespace reservations.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only reservation map and duplicate marker over a tiny in-memory counter domain with no live cryptographic traffic or external state.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate allocator generation, worker identities, reservation ranges, namespace/key scope, duplicated final value, consumer calls, and deterministic receipts.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold workers, schedule, namespace, key scope, consumer, and requested range sizes constant while changing only overlapping versus atomic disjoint reservation allocation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject independent namespaces, unconsumed overlap, duplicate logging, counter wrap, stale persistence state, fork clone, or encoding collapse as alternative causes.
scenarios.evidence_level: NRL3 because mock consumers accept one duplicate counter-derived nonce twice in the same synthetic security scope after overlapping reservations are consumed.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: NRL3 maximum until a bounded reversible construction-state effect plus complete allocator/concurrency/remediation provenance justifies NRL4 or NRL5.

scenarios.hypothesis: Two distinct raw synthetic random values become the same final security-relevant value after deterministic truncation or encoding and are both consumed in one required uniqueness scope.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A deterministic fake generator and mock read-only consumer compare only synthetic raw and encoded values, producing an inert collision receipt with no real tokens or secrets.
scenarios.positive_control: Using the full-width final value or a sufficiently wide collision-resistant encoding preserves distinct consumer identities for the same two raw synthetic values.
scenarios.negative_control: A display-only truncated label collides while the mock security consumer still receives distinct full-width values, proving presentation collisions are not automatically security collisions.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture would expose production tokens, leave the local owned sandbox, require live prediction against real systems, or use unauthorized secrets.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After widening or domain-separating the consumed representation, the same deterministic raw pair no longer collapses under the actual security consumer equality rule.
scenarios.value_property_security_scope: Classify the final value as an identifier or nonce requiring uniqueness in one synthetic security scope and record whether the requirement applies after transformation.
scenarios.generator_seed_entropy_reseed: Use a deterministic generator fixture with distinct raw outputs and fixed seed/reseed state so the collision is attributable to the transform rather than generator repetition.
scenarios.fork_snapshot_restart_lifecycle: Hold process, fork, snapshot, and restart generations constant and absent so lifecycle cloning cannot explain the final-value collision.
scenarios.counter_namespace_reservation: Record that no counter namespace or reservation layer participates in this case, isolating the transform/encoding domain as the only changed causal dimension.
scenarios.persistence_crash_restart: Keep persistence state unused and constant; no restored checkpoint or crash/restart transition occurs during generation or consumption of the two values.
scenarios.transform_encoding_truncation: Bind both distinct raw value identities, truncation/encoding operation, output width, canonical equality domain, and the identical final consumed value.
scenarios.consumer_construction_identity: Identify the mock final consumer and its equality semantics, proving it consumes the truncated/encoded value rather than a separate unique full-width representation.
scenarios.effective_randomness_lifecycle_capabilit: The demonstrated capability is limited to deterministic same-scope collision of two final synthetic values caused solely by the security-relevant transform.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is an inert collision receipt containing both raw values and the shared transformed value; no token authority or cryptographic exploit is attempted.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate generator generation, two raw outputs, transform identity, security scope, final duplicate value, consumer equality decision, and collision receipt.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold generator, raw pair, scope, and consumer constant while changing only security-relevant full-width versus truncated/encoded final representation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject display-only collision, underlying raw duplicate, different consumer scopes, encoding aliases that remain semantically distinct, or hidden domain-separation fields.
scenarios.evidence_level: NRL3 because a mock security consumer accepts the same transformed final value twice from distinct raw synthetic values in one required uniqueness scope.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: NRL3 maximum until a bounded reversible construction effect and complete transform/consumer/remediation provenance justify stronger NRL4 or NRL5 evidence.
